summary.headline: AVG Logistics Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 39% QoQ... more precisely PAT up 39.2% YoY to ₹7.1 crore on revenue up 6% to ₹151.6 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was ₹151.6 crore, up 6% YoY and 14.4% QoQ, while reported EBITDA (including other income) fell 10.3% YoY to ₹23.6 crore on a lease-accounting reclassification. Management attributed the EBITDA decline mainly to lease rentals moving from depreciation and finance cost into operating expenses, and pointed to PBT and PAT growth (PAT up 39.2% YoY to ₹7.1 crore) as the better measure. H1 FY27 revenue was ₹284.1 crore (up 6%), with PAT up about 33-39% depending on basis. Management said new contracts (Ram/Dalmia electric fleet, liquor logistics) only contributed for part of the quarter and will show fuller benefit from Q3, and reiterated 15-20% growth guidance for FY27.

segments.name: Liquor logistics (new)
segments.commentary: Entered July 2026 with long-term contracts with two liquor companies; expected FY27 revenue about ₹24 crore, targeting about ₹100 crore from next year. Management says six to seven prospects are in the pipeline across beer and whisky.

segments.name: Cement / heavy-duty electric trucks (North East contract)
segments.commentary: Five-year contract signed August 2026 (extendable by three years) with a cement company; 30 heavy electric trucks (38-41 tonnes, about 50 trips per month each) now in service in Assam.

segments.name: Multimodal project contract
segments.commentary: Five-year transportation contract worth about ₹60 crore signed in November 2026 with a global company for product movement, per management.

segments.name: Ram/Dalmia and Haldiram FMCG contracts
segments.commentary: Ram/Dalmia fleet started August/September 2026; Haldiram rollout expected to total about ₹28-32 crore annual revenue once 100 vehicles are on road. Full benefit expected from Q3.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20%, which management said implies double-digit growth in H2 as Q1/Q2 are seasonally weaker.
FY27 PBT guided at ₹34-35 crore vs ₹26 crore last year.
Vision 2030 target of ₹250 crore revenue (per transcript; figure stated inconsistently) and about 120 crore by 2030 mentioned; management also cited a 10% EBITDA margin ambition.
Plan to add about 200-250 electric vehicles by March 2027 using a mix of buy and lease models.
Management expects new fleets and contracts to contribute fully in H2 FY27.
capex_capacity: Plan to add about 200-250 electric vehicles by March 2027, funded through a mix of buying and operating leases (including a lease tie-up with a financier).
Charging stations cost about ₹1 crore each; 4-5 chargers planned at origin and destination for the Ram/Dalmia electric route; charger host is the customer, which provided site space.
Fleet is about 1,100 vehicles (management) versus over 3,000 owned and hired vehicles cited elsewhere in the call; 70 branches and about 7.5 lakh sq ft warehousing.
New Khorla (Odisha) facility targeted for next financial year, dependent on customer factory/warehouse development in the industrial area.
Land already acquired in Himachal Pradesh and Odisha for FMCG, warehousing and part-load/express services.
demand_pricing: About 75-80% of business is under contracts with fuel-price pass-through formulas (diesel roughly 40-45% of freight cost); pass-through lag is 10-15 days.
Management says FY27 margin pressure from fuel spike in H1 was largely managed; the Ram/Dalmia and new contracts started late in H1, so full impact comes in Q3.
Cement and steel customers under carbon-reduction pressure are signing long-term electric-truck contracts; management says more cement customers are in discussion.
Management said acquisition targets are asking for valuations of around 1.5x turnover, which it considers unreasonable.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY27 revenue reach the 15-20% guidance when H1 growth was in single digits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 and Q2 are seasonally weaker; the Ram/Dalmia fleet (started August) and Dalmia (September) contracts contributed only for part of H1 and will run full quarters from October, with more contracts being implemented in November-December. Management expects double-digit growth in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA/PBT outlook after the Ind AS lease change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the reported EBITDA decline reflects reclassification of lease rentals into operating expenses; PBT for FY27 is expected at ₹34-35 crore vs ₹26 crore last year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue size of the Haldiram and Ram/Dalmia contracts at full run-rate and their margin relative to FMCG?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined annual revenue of about ₹28-32 crore once the 100 vehicles are fully deployed; management said electric and CNG vehicles yield better margins than diesel.

qa_highlights.question: Expected capex, buy vs lease split and leverage by March?
qa_highlights.answer: Plan to add 200-250 electric vehicles by March 2027 using both buy and lease; management stated debt is comfortable and cited debt of about ₹120 crore plus at March (per management).

qa_highlights.question: How much liquor logistics revenue is expected and from how many customers?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹25 crore in FY27 from four customers in the first year; target of about ₹100 crore per year, with six to seven liquor companies in the pipeline (two already signed).

qa_highlights.question: Borrowings and use of right-issue proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the ₹189 crore borrowing figure, saying borrowings rose ₹30-40 crore; about 25% of proceeds went to general corporate purposes and the rest mainly to working capital; capex funded through 5-7 year debt. Management said borrowings were about ₹120 crore plus at March.

risks_watch: Reported EBITDA fell 10.3% YoY in Q2 and 11% in H1 due to lease reclassification; comparability of EBITDA across periods needs to be checked.
Consolidated revenue growth in H1 (6%) is well below the 15-20% FY27 guidance; H2 must deliver double-digit growth.
Borrowing levels: management disputed the ₹189 crore figure raised on the call; actual debt levels and net debt should be verified in the filing.
Pass-through lag of 10-15 days on fuel and the 20-25% uncovered business exposure to diesel price moves.
Acquisition valuations and execution risk on the 2030 targets (inconsistent figures given on the call: ₹250 crore vs ₹1,250 crore, and 10% margin target).
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, electric-fleet contracts and margin expansion, but noticeably defensive on the reported EBITDA decline and the debt question. Several figures were restated or corrected during the call, so guidance numbers should be verified against the filing.
key_quotes: Since most of our business is under contract, fuel price changes its factors for less directly at that same time growing part of our fleet now runs on CNG, LNG and electric.
For a like for like view of the business profit before test is better is a better measure.
We remain committed to the objective we say shared on our last call we delivering around 15 to 20 percent growth year in or 20 year 27.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth of 15-20% reiterated (midpoint 17.5%), with H2 double-digit growth implied; backed by 200-250 EV additions by March 2027, a ~Rs 60 crore multimodal contract, Haldiram rollout (Rs 28-32 crore annual revenue at 100 vehicles) and liquor logistics (~Rs 24 crore FY27), but H1 revenue grew only 6% and the EV fleet and Khorla facility lack firm timing or capex figures.

oneOffs.what: Ind AS lease reclassification moved lease rentals from depreciation and finance cost into operating expenses, lowering reported EBITDA (down 10.3% YoY to ₹23.6 cr) while lifting PBT/PAT comparability

quality.why: Q2 revenue grew only 6% YoY to ₹151.6 cr, with the brief giving no quantified volume or price split, and PAT growth of 39% is flattered by the Ind AS lease reclassification that moved rentals out of depreciation and finance cost, while reported EBITDA fell 10.3%; new contracts (Ram/Dalmia, liquor logistics) only partly contributed in the quarter, so the recurring top-line growth is low single digi

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin rose to 6.7% from 4.5% YoY and PAT margin to 4.7% from 3.5%, with FY27 PBT guided at ₹34-35 crore vs ₹26 crore, but reported consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 15.6% from 18.4% on lease reclassification and fuel pass-through lags of 10-15 days remain.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Plan to add 200-250 EVs by March 2027 (buy plus lease, with a financier lease tie-up) against a fleet of about 1,100 vehicles per management, though the EV count is not yet tied to a firm capex figure and the Khorla facility is only targeted for next financial year.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth of 15-20% reiterated, implying double-digit H2 growth after H1 revenue grew only 6% to ₹284.1 crore, supported by the Ram/Dalmia fleet running full quarters from October, the ~₹60 crore multimodal contract and Haldiram rollout worth ₹28-32 crore annually at 100 vehicles.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Land already acquired in Himachal Pradesh and Odisha and the Khorla facility is targeted for next financial year, but no utilisation figure was given and the call gave no firm capex amount beyond EV additions and chargers at about ₹1 crore each.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was held at 15-20% FY27 growth after H1 revenue growth of just 6%, so management is not signalling a raise and H2 must deliver double-digit growth just to reach the range.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue grew 6% against a 15-20% FY27 target, the new contracts only ramp from Q3, and borrowings were disputed (₹189 crore raised vs management's ~₹120 crore plus), so a miss on H2 delivery is a real risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Liquor logistics entered July 2026 with two signed contracts targeting about ₹24 crore in FY27 and ~₹100 crore from next year, with six to seven prospects in the pipeline.

rows.label: Multimodal ₹60 crore five-year contract
rows.why: Five-year transportation contract worth about ₹60 crore signed with a global company, roughly ₹12 crore a year on average over the contract life.

rows.label: Liquor logistics ramp to ₹100 crore
rows.why: About ₹24-25 crore expected in FY27 from four customers and a ₹100 crore target next year, but this depends on converting six to seven pipeline prospects.

rows.label: Debt levels disputed
rows.why: Management put borrowings at about ₹120 crore plus at March and disputed the ₹189 crore figure, while capex is funded via 5-7 year debt, so net debt needs checking against the filing.

tone.note: Management was confident on the electric-fleet contracts, the 15-20% FY27 growth guide and standalone margin expansion, but defensive on the reported consolidated EBITDA decline and the borrowings figure; analysts pressed on how H1 single-digit growth reaches the guidance.
